name: TSV912IDT
title: TSV91x and TSV91xA: single, dual and quad 8 MHz op amps with rail-to-rail inputs and outputs
summary: A family of op amps in one, two and four channels (TSV911, TSV912, TSV914) for 2.5 V to 5.5 V supplies, with inputs and outputs that both reach the rails. Each channel draws 0.78 mA typical and 1.1 mA at most, gives 8 MHz of gain-bandwidth and 4.5 V/µs, is stable at unity gain, and has an input bias current of 1 pA typical. The A grade holds offset to 1.5 mV at 25 °C against 4.5 mV for the standard grade. TSV912IDT is the standard-grade dual in an 8-pin SO package on tape and reel.
key_figures: 27 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz, 21 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz (5 V)

notes: Voltages are taken from the ground terminal of the network, apart from the differential input voltage.
The differential input voltage is the non-inverting input measured against the inverting input.
VCC - VIN may not go above 6 V.
A series resistor at each input has to hold the input current within its rating.
A shorted output can dissipate enough heat to destroy the part.
The thermal resistances are typical figures.
HBM: a 100 pF capacitor discharged through 1.5 kΩ between each pair of pins in turn, every other pin open.
MM: a 200 pF capacitor charged to the rated voltage and discharged straight between each pair of pins in turn, with no series resistor added (under 5 Ω inside), every other pin open.
CDM: all pins and the package charged together to the rated voltage, then discharged straight to ground.

operation.text: The amplifiers run from 2.5 V to 5.5 V across -40 °C to 125 °C; from 0 °C upward the lower limit drops to 2.3 V. The absolute maximum supply is 6 V.

The common-mode range extends 0.1 V past both supply rails. The pins themselves are rated to 0.2 V past either rail and to 10 mA; a resistor in series with each input keeps the current inside that figure. The differential input may span the full supply.
The part is aimed at loads of 2 kΩ and higher. The output swings within 15 mV typical (40 mV max) of each rail into 10 kΩ and within 45 mV typical (150 mV max) into 600 Ω.

As a voltage follower the amplifier stays free of oscillation with up to 100 pF on its output. For heavier capacitance a small resistor in series with the output restores stability; the smallest such resistor that holds peaking to 2.3 dB or less falls from about 36 Ω at 300 pF to about 4 Ω at 100 nF (VCC = 5 V). A chosen value is then confirmed in simulation and on the bench.
Each supply pin gets a 10 nF decoupling capacitor placed as close to the pin as possible.
The DFN8 2x2 exposed pad has no internal connection. It may be tied to VCC- or left open.

With the output pulled to the opposite rail it supplies 35 mA typical (18 mA min) when sourcing and 32 mA typical (18 mA min) when sinking at 25 °C. Shorting the output can heat the die to the point of destructive dissipation.

A TSV91x macromodel is available from ST. It represents a typical device inside the rated operating conditions and is meant for selecting the amplifier and checking a design; measurements on the real board still decide.
Order codes with Y in the suffix are automotive grade: qualified and characterized to AEC Q100 and Q003 or equivalent, with advanced screening to AEC Q001 and Q002 or equivalent.
